output:
To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: So, um, I started a business

Ok. Deep breath. I've rewritten the first line of this like six times so I'm just going to say it.

I'm going out on my own. Fernhollow Photo is a real, actual business now, with paperwork and a website and everything. I wanted you guys to hear it from me here first, and not halfway through Ruthie's turkey.

Here's the backstory. Marisol told me on October 6 that she was closing Rosebud Lane, and the studio officially closed at the end of October. I shot for her for four years. Some of you have heard me talk about her, but probably not enough. She basically taught me everything. How to read a room. How to get eighty people into a group shot without anyone crying. How to stay calm when the bride's veil blows into a lake (Hood River, 2024, we got it back). When I started I was a girl with a decent eye and no idea how to run a wedding day. Most of what I know now, I know because of her. So Marisol, if you ever see this, thank you. Really.

When she told me, the first thing she did was say she'd be referring her 2027 couples to me. She'd already told six of them I was the one. And she said something I keep thinking about, which was that I've been ready for two years.

The funny part is she's right, because I've been planning this in my head for about two years. I had a whole imaginary business with a name and a logo and a pricing sheet I'd fiddle with on the MAX. I just figured I'd do it "someday." Turns out someday was October.

**The part where I prove I'm not being reckless**

I know some of you (hi Dad) are already worried, so here are the facts:

- **14 weddings are already booked for 2027.** Six came from Marisol's referrals and eight are couples who found me on their own. Deposits are already coming in.
- **Health insurance is handled.** DAD. I picked a marketplace plan on November 5 and it starts January 1. I have health insurance. You don't have to do the speech. I love you. Please don't do the speech.
- **I'm not doing the big weddings alone.** My friend Jae will second shoot the big ones with me and gets paid per wedding. So nobody's chasing two flower girls at once, which matters, because you all know how the lens cap thing went.
- The LLC is filed (Fernhollow Photo LLC, as of October 22) and the website went live November 1.

Is it scary? Yeah, honestly, it's a little scary. I'm not going to pretend it isn't. But it's scary like jumping into the river at the cabin, not scary like being lost in the woods. I know where I'm going and I have a plan. Most of it is already on a calendar.

**The first one that was all mine**

I have to tell you about this because it's the moment it felt real.

On Friday I got an email from a couple named Dahlia and Ken. They're getting married at Timberline Lodge on June 12, and they booked me. They didn't come through Rosebud Lane or a referral. They found my photos of one of Marisol's couples at Multnomah Falls, and Dahlia wrote that "that's what sold us."

I read it in the kitchen and then I read it out loud to Sam and Pickle. Pickle was not impressed. Sam was. A wedding at Timberline, on a mountain, in June, because someone liked my pictures. I'm still kind of floating.

**Things that happened that I'm including for honesty**

I filed the LLC on my lunch break, sitting in my car in a Fred Meyer parking lot. I hit submit and cried a little. Not sad crying, more "oh no, I'm a grown up" crying. A guy pushing a cart of paper towels definitely saw me. We made eye contact. I'm sure he's fine.

Then Sam made me a cake to celebrate. It was beautiful and it said FERNHOLOW. One L. I didn't notice for about ten minutes, and then I couldn't stop laughing, and he claimed he "ran out of room on the cake." We ate it anyway and it was delicious. Honestly I think the misspelled cake should be the official logo.

**Why "Fernhollow" (Grandma, this part is for you)**

Some of you might already have guessed. The name is from the fern hollow trail behind Grandma's old place in Gresham.

That's where I took my first real pictures, with Grandma's Pentax. I was maybe eleven or twelve and she let me carry it down the trail. I remember being so scared of dropping it that I walked like I was holding a bowl of soup. I took a whole roll of ferns, a slug, a blurry squirrel, and one picture of Grandma laughing at me that she still says is a bad picture. It isn't. It's one of my favorites.

So Grandma, the name is for you. You put a camera in my hands, let me wander off down the trail with it, and never once acted like it was a waste of film. Everything I'm doing now started back there. I wanted you to know that, and I wanted everyone else to know too.

**Ok now the fun part: Thanksgiving**

I'm bringing my camera to Ruthie's on the 26th (along with the rolls and the cranberry thing, Mom, I didn't forget). If anybody wants family pictures, I'll do them for free. That means couples, kids, your whole branch of the family, or just you looking cute next to the pie table. Comment below or grab me when I get there and we'll find good light before it gets dark. Dinner's at 3, so the earlier the better for outdoor ones.

I promise I'll be faster than the Christmas group photo. Uncle Greg, you won't freeze this time. Probably.

Also, little Juniper, I know you aren't receiving visitors until after Thanksgiving, but your auntie's camera will be ready whenever your parents say so. Bree, no pressure, just putting it out there.

**Last thing**

I know a lot of you have been quietly hoping I'd find something with "steady hours." I get it, and I know it comes from love. But this is the thing I'm good at and the thing I love, and I finally have the bookings, the plan, and the guts to do it for real. I'd love for you to be excited with me.

Love you all. See you in Salem. Bring your good sweaters.

Tessa
Fernhollow Photo (two Ls, Sam)

reasons: The draft says Dahlia's email arrived Friday, but it is dated Saturday, November 7.
